newsitem.title: USA: U.S. teen charged in "vampire" case appears in court.
newsitem.headline: U.S. teen charged in "vampire" case appears in court.

text.p: The first of five teenagers from a self-styled "vampire clan" was ordered held without bail on murder charges during her first appearance in court on Wednesday.

Dana Lynn Cooper, 19, and her four co-defendants were all arrested Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 28, in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, for the murder of a Eustis, Florida, couple, Richard and Ruth Wendorf, parents of one of the teenagers.
The youths were thought to be members of a tightly knit, secretive group suspected of sucking blood from small animals and each other in graveyard rituals.
As the only adult in the group, Cooper was brought back to Florida before the others, who faced a separate extradition hearing on Wednesday before a Louisiana judge.

Cooper appeared pale and withdrawn at the Lake County jail and answered questions from County Judge Donna Miller. She was assigned a public defender and will enter a plea at her arraignment, following a grand jury presentment.
Prosecutors have not announced whether they would seek the death penalty in the deaths of the central Florida couple.

The other teenagers, Heather Wendorf, 15 and the dead couple's youngest daughter, Roderick Ferrell, 16, who was the alleged ringleader, Howard Scott Anderson, 16, and Sara Remington, 16, were being treated as juveniles in Louisiana, but were to be tried as adults in Florida, prosecutor Bill Stone said.

Wendorf was the only Floridian in the group. Her connection to the others, all from rural Kentucky, was through Ferrell, who organised as many as 40 Kentucky youths into a vampire clan, authorities said.

Investigators have said that Ferrell, who used the "vampire name" Vesago, wanted Heather, called Zoey, to marry Anderson, called Nash. They speculated that the Wendorfs' refusal to allow their daughter to marry may have been a motive in their murder.
